introHeading: Editorial portraits for Long Island's black-tie evenings
introParas: Long Island's dressiest events — a black-tie wedding on a Gold Coast estate, a summer gala in the Hamptons, a milestone birthday at a Nassau country club — tend to bring guests who made an effort, and the glam booth's black-and-white editorial look is built to match it. Our studio lighting rig renders skin tones evenly regardless of how many guests have already come through, which matters at the larger receptions Long Island venues routinely host.

It's also a booth we treat differently once the setup moves outdoors, which happens more on Long Island than in most of the city — a Hamptons tent, a mansion's covered terrace, a lawn ceremony that flows straight into the reception. Because the glam look depends on our own studio-powered lighting rather than ambient light, we can hold the same black-and-white edit outdoors as indoors, provided the site is sheltered from wind and rain. We confirm that with you well before the date.

Setup wants 10ft x 10ft for the backdrop and prop table, compressing to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of clearance for a tighter Nassau hall floor, plus a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet, which we run ourselves rather than sharing a circuit. Because the drive out to Long Island runs longer than a Brooklyn booking, travel is quoted from your venue's exact ZIP code before you book rather than folded into a flat borough rate — nothing to discover on the invoice afterward.

faqHeading: Glam Photo Booth on Long Island — FAQ

faqs.q: Is there a travel fee for the glam booth on Long Island?
faqs.a: There's no flat rate the way there is closer to Brooklyn. Travel across Nassau, Suffolk and the Hamptons is quoted from your venue's exact ZIP code before you book, so you know the real number ahead of time.

faqs.q: Can the glam booth handle a large Gold Coast or Nassau hall wedding?
faqs.a: Yes — unlimited sessions and unlimited prints mean guest count isn't a ceiling. For very large receptions we often suggest pairing the glam booth with a roaming attendant or a second station so the line stays short through cocktail hour.

faqs.q: Can the glam booth be set up under a tent at a Hamptons event?
faqs.a: Yes. Because the glam look comes from our own studio-powered lighting rather than ambient light, we can hold the same black-and-white edit under a tent as indoors, provided the site is level, dry and sheltered from wind. We'll confirm the details with you before booking.

faqs.q: How much space does the glam booth need at a Long Island venue?
faqs.a: 10ft x 10ft is optimal for the backdrop, prop table and a red-carpet feel; we can compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for tighter rooms.

faqs.q: Is color available, or is it black-and-white only?
faqs.a: Both — the black-and-white glam edit is the signature look, but the booth can output color, black-and-white, or let each guest choose.

faqs.q: What power do you need at a Nassau or Suffolk venue?
faqs.a: A standard 110V, 5-amp, 3-prong outlet within 15 feet of the booth. We bring our own dedicated power run rather than sharing a circuit with a tent's lighting or a DJ setup.
Yes — we can dial it up for a full editorial look or keep it subtle so guests still look like themselves. Tell us your preference before the event and we'll set it in advance.

faqs.q: Can you send a certificate of insurance for a Long Island venue that requires one?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy — reply to your booking confirmation with the venue's contact and we will send it over.

faqs.q: How much lead time do you build in for a Long Island booking?
faqs.a: More than we would for a Brooklyn venue. Because the LIE and Hamptons summer traffic are real variables, we schedule a wider arrival window for Long Island so we're still on site a full hour before your start time regardless of the drive.
